query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small interstitial concentration of nitrogen via plasma nitriding will induce a controlled tetragonal distortion in the fcc FeCoNi matrix, thereby increasing its magnetic anisotropy and enhancing the coercive field relative to the untreated material.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi (or its high-entropy alloy derivative) exhibiting a coercive field near 100 Oe
generation.intervention: Apply plasma nitriding under moderate conditions to incorporate interstitial nitrogen into the alloy
generation.conditions: Nitriding performed at temperatures low enough (around 400–500 °C) to avoid forming secondary phases, with controlled exposure to yield a small, uniform nitrogen incorporation
generation.structural_mediator: Lattice tetragonal distortion induced by the interstitial nitrogen in the predominantly fcc matrix
generation.mechanism: The induced lattice distortion increases the magnetic anisotropy of the material, which enhances domain wall pinning during magnetization reversal, thus increasing the coercive field
generation.predicted_outcome: The treated material is predicted to exhibit a coercive field significantly higher than 100 Oe (potentially a 50% increase or greater over the untreated state) while largely retaining its high saturation magnetization
generation.baseline: Untreated single-phase fcc FeCoNi (or derivative) with a coercive field of approximately 100 Oe at room temperature
generation.boundary: Measurements conducted at room temperature on samples with similar dimensions and processing histories; composition maintained near stoichiometric FeCoNi without other alloying additions that could independently alter magnetism
generation.uncertainty: The precise magnitude of the coercivity increase is uncertain and may depend on the degree and uniformity of nitrogen incorporation as well as potential local microstructural inhomogeneities

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of single-phase fcc FeCoNi processed under standard conditions (control) and another set subjected to plasma nitriding at controlled 400–500 °C conditions. Perform X-ray diffraction (XRD) to detect any lattice distortion (e.g., shifts or splitting indicative of tetragonality) and magnetic hysteresis measurements using Vibrating Sample Magnetometry (VSM) to quantify coercivity.
measurements: XRD analysis to assess lattice parameter modifications and detect any induced tetragonal distortion
VSM measurements to obtain hysteresis loops and determine coercive fields for both control and nitrided samples
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the nitrided samples do not exhibit a statistically significant increase in coercive field (e.g., an increase of at least 50% over the control) and measurable lattice distortion compared to untreated samples, then the hypothesis that interstitial nitrogen induced by plasma nitriding overcomes the coercivity limitation is falsified.
